Uncertainty: the described geometry alone does not clearly establish that contact. The clear appearance of milk does not prove safety, but proximity alone also does not prove contamination. Clarify the observed exposure before claiming a unique key.
The sequence is coherent: drainage supplies the MRSA culture and the new task supplies feeding observations. No earlier explanation teaches the answer.
The broader breastfeeding/MRSA principle has practical value; this intricate flange-contact scenario is not established here as a commonly tested ABSITE concept.
suggestions: Replace the ambiguous aperture geometry with a short direct observation of whether milk or milk-contact pump parts touch infected tissue or drainage; retain the separate covered direct-latch observation.
Limit disposal to milk from the described exposure and identify reassessment/clean repositioning as subsequent care in feedback, without inventing a universal withholding interval.
Keep the balanced option matrix. A simple original schematic could aid clarity only if its actual visible observations are independently reviewed.
